title: Short-horizon gauge robustness
question: Are the weak-field Nulloth scalar amplitude and active-versus-control geometric response robust between harmonic and 1+log slicing while the coordinate lapse responds to the gauge choice?
prediction: The scalar amplitude and physical-metric contrast differ by less than 0.2 percent between slicings, while the lapse contrast differs by more than 25 percent. All conservation, entropy, constraint, convexity, and recovery vetoes pass.
falsifier: A primary-observable spread above tolerance, an insensitive lapse control, failed conservation or entropy account, constraint violation, nonpositive convexity margin, or recovery failure falsifies the short-horizon robustness claim.
controls: Harmonic and 1+log pairs share matter, carrier modulation, scalar seed, gravity coupling, grid, time step, and duration.
Each active state is compared to an independently constraint-solved scalar-free control under the same slicing.
Scalar amplitude and physical-metric contrast are primary observables; lapse contrast is the gauge-sensitive control.
Constraint, conservation, entropy, convexity, and recovery accounts are evaluated independently.
